reference_policy.use: scope/structure/terminology/difficulty/fidelity calibration only; proprietary wording is not copied
reference_policy.note: The high-trace-load rubric and floor proposed below are FE QUEST internal quality controls, not an official IPA item ratio.

runtime_inventory.history_fairness: seen count is considered before current-session format frequency; random tie break follows

high_trace_load_rubric.purpose: Identify items that require sustained reconstruction of dependent state rather than a local one-line operation.
criteria: at least three dependent state transitions or a non-linear recursive/data-structure traversal must be reconstructed
the answer depends on the sequence of state changes rather than one isolated operator or one direct blank
the item evolves multiple variables or a structured state such as an array, queue, pointer chain, search interval or recursion tree

contract_valid_low_trace_probe.history_setup: Give these 16 items the lowest seen count and make high-trace alternatives older in priority only after a much larger seen count; because seen is the first selector key, these candidates can dominate their compatible pools.
contract_valid_low_trace_probe.assessment: A final algorithm session can satisfy the current structural contracts while containing no item that meets the v207 sustained-state rubric. This promotes the v204 context-density watch from Low to Medium at the integrated-session level.

medium.evidence: The 40-item pool has 12 manually classified high-trace-load items, but final selection does not use this dimension. A contract-valid 8-standard/8-applied, ten-domain, unique-ID construction exists with zero high-trace-load items under an adversarial but valid exposure history.
medium.impact: A readiness check can have excellent breadth and format balance yet under-sample sustained state tracking, making some generated final sessions materially lighter than the skill the Subject B practice is intended to measure.
medium.repair_boundary: Selection policy only. Preserve all question wording and IDs, 20=16+4, ten-domain representation, standard8/applied8, unique IDs, security selection, review/diagnosis and saved history.

v208_recommendation.conditional: apply only when quota-compatible unused high-trace candidates exist
v208_recommendation.policy_note: The value 4 is an FE QUEST internal readiness floor, not an official exam composition claim.
preserve: seen-history fairness within compatible candidate classes
